subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept the Codex Action v1.11 runner preparation that disables Ubuntu's AppArmor restriction on unprivileged user namespaces before dropping sudo?
rationale: The upstream action deliberately changes a host-level sandbox prerequisite in workflows that receive repository contents and API secrets; correctness tests cannot decide whether that security tradeoff matches OpenClaw's policy.

options.title: Approve after secops review
options.body: Keep the grouped pin update, document secops approval of the Codex runner preparation, refresh the branch, and require green exact-head checks.

options.title: Split the Codex bump
options.body: Land the other action updates separately and review the Codex Action change in a focused security-owned PR.

options.title: Hold the grouped update
options.body: Leave all pins unchanged until a different Codex sandbox setup avoids the host user-namespace policy change.

recommendation.title: Approve after secops review
recommendation.body: Keep the grouped pin update, document secops approval of the Codex runner preparation, refresh the branch, and require green exact-head checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The history most strongly connects this person to the affected CI, Docker release, and Codex-powered docs-agent workflow surfaces.
